manualReview.scope: Model/editor semantic and pedagogy review of the current Lesson 0024 source; not an independent human or learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: Is this your book/pen? and It's my book/pen. are natural short ownership exchanges in the classroom cleanup context.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Learner-facing Persian accurately distinguishes your from my; ownership questions now use «مال توست؟» instead of «توئه؟», preserving meaning while matching Nova orthography rules.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: No new lexical word is added; the lesson isolates the my/your ownership contrast using two already-known objects.

distractorQuality.evidence: The ownership choice contrasts my, your and an unrelated-but-recent read statement, requiring role/meaning awareness rather than only noun recognition.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: Sorting books and pens after class naturally motivates repeated questions about whose object each item is.

difficultyFit.evidence: Known object vocabulary makes a two-construction grammar contrast manageable for early A1 without extra lexical load.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: Book and pen return for a new grammatical function after prior possession and reading contexts, providing useful spaced reuse.

transferQuality.evidence: The learner moves from have-based possession language to my/your ownership and then recombines the frame with pen in hidden-answer retrieval.

overallCoherence.evidence: Scenario, dialogue, reconstruction, ownership contrast and final speaking task all serve the same my/your outcome with no unnecessary vocabulary.

learnerExperience.evidence: Static flow review only; the progression is clear and low-load, but real learner errors on my versus your and speech-recognition behavior are not yet measured.

limitations: No independent human or learner testing has been performed.
The lesson covers only bounded ownership with familiar concrete nouns, not the full possessive system.
Final audio/prosody and delayed retention remain untested.
resolvedFindings: Removed non-word formula entries from the lexical word layer; the ownership forms remain constructions rather than fake vocabulary.
No new lexical target is introduced, preserving a consolidation cadence after Lessons 21–23.
The final retrieval changes the object and requires productive reuse of It's my + item.
Persian ownership questions were normalized from توئه to مال توست without changing the English target or activity logic.
